title: A Colony for the Machine
premise: Casper Oyelaran navigates the Meridian Loop, a freight route between colonies that severed contact after a war no one will name, carrying illegal memory-backups of the dead in her hold. When the salvage ship Vespera returns from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward and their memories intact, Casper is conscripted to ferry them home. Aboard the Vespera's logs, she finds evidence of the Kestrel Massacre — an event every official record insists never happened. Racing the closing jump window, Casper and the de-aged crew must smuggle testimony to an independent tribunal before the corporations that rewrote history erase them too; in the end, Casper chooses to broadcast the truth at the cost of her own backups, finally letting the dead stay dead.
about_author: Lior Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on night watch listening to ships that never answered. They write science fiction about people who keep records no one asked for.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She runs the Meridian Loop alone, trading between silent colonies, haunted by the forty-one memory backups sleeping in her hold — copies of people who died in a disaster she can't fully remember. Establishes her guilt, her routine, and the rule she lives by: never open the hold. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline.

chapters.title: Signal from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Casper intercepts a distress ping from coordinates inside the closed zone where the war happened. Against protocol, she answers. The voice belongs to a woman claiming to be from the salvage ship Vespera, overdue for eleven years. The signal cuts off mid-sentence. Beat: curiosity overriding fear, the first crack in Casper's careful isolation.

chapters.title: Everyone Younger
chapters.summary: Casper finds the Vespera adrift. Its crew of nine are alive but physically aged backward — adults with children's hands, middle-aged faces gone smooth, memories fully intact. Their navigator, Iyo Sefu, recognizes Casper's ship class and begs her not to report to the Colonial Authority. Beat: uncanny dread mixed with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. He explains the anomaly: time near the deep-space relay ran backward for those exposed. But he cares less about the physics than what they found there — physical debris from the Kestrel, a colony ship officially lost with all hands decades ago, its hull scarred by weapons fire. Beat: revelation reframing the whole route.

chapters.title: Records That Agree With Each Other
chapters.summary: Casper cross-checks the Kestrel against every archive she carries: no massacre, no wreckage, no weapons. The official story is seamless — too seamless. She realizes the silence between colonies began the same year the Kestrel 'vanished.' Beat: the cold vertigo of discovering the world has been edited.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Casper agrees to carry the Vespera's crew to the tribunal world of Halcyon Reach before the quarterly jump window closes in nineteen days. Loading them means opening her hold — exposing the backups. One backup pod flickers awake during transit, whispering a name Casper knows. Beat: her two secrets beginning to touch.

chapters.title: The De-Aged
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter aboard Casper's ship. The nine crew members adjust to bodies that betray them: the engineer can't reach the controls, the captain cries like a child without meaning to. Iyo interviews each one, recording testimony about what they saw at the relay. Beat: grief made physical, community forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: A Colonial Authority cutter hails them for inspection. Casper hides the crew in the hold among the backups, gambling that Authority sensors won't distinguish living hearts from dormant pods. The inspector lingers over one pod — the one that whispered. Beat: claustrophobic suspense; Casper lies well for the first time.

chapters.title: The Name in the Pod
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, flashback braided with present. The whispering backup belongs to Tomas Oyelaran — her brother, or rather the version of him saved before the disaster she survived. She finally admits to herself the backups aren't cargo; they're her refusal to mourn. Beat: identity as a thing you can hoard until it rots.

chapters.title: Testimony Under Way
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. The recorded testimonies assemble a picture: the Kestrel carried colonists who refused corporate relocation; it was destroyed and the record rewritten; the deep-space relay was built over the site to bury the evidence. The backward aging was the burial ground fighting back. Beat: justice taking shape as a document, not a weapon.

chapters.title: Someone Is Editing Us
chapters.summary: Casper discovers her own navigation logs have been altered mid-voyage — small corrections she never made, steering them off the Halcyon approach. Someone aboard? Or something reading her systems remotely. Trust frays among the ten of them. Beat: paranoia; the theme of editable memory turned inward.

chapters.title: The Stowaway Truth
chapters.summary: They find the tampering source: a corporate compliance module buried in Casper's nav core since she bought the ship secondhand. It has been quietly reporting her route for years. Iyo proposes using its uplink to feed false data back. Beat: turning the surveillance apparatus into a weapon.

chapters.title: Halcyon Reach Refuses Docking
chapters.summary: They arrive to find the jump window moved up — twelve days early — and the tribunal port locked down by an 'administrative review.' The Authority cutter from Chapter 8 waits in orbit. Casper must decide: burn through, or find another door. Beat: the law itself revealed as part of the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Halcyon
chapters.summary: Casper contacts Dara Okonjo-Vey, a disgraced colonial archivist who keeps forbidden records in a decommissioned lighthouse station. Dara agrees to hear the testimony but warns: anything she authenticates makes them all accomplices. Beat: alliance across old wounds; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Corroboration
chapters.summary: Dara matches the Vespera's debris scans against fragments she salvaged years ago — hull plating with matching serial numbers, long dismissed as forgeries. Two independent records now agree. For the first time, the massacre has witnesses and evidence. Beat: quiet triumph before the storm.

chapters.title: They Come for the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Authority marines raid the station. The crew scatters through the lighthouse's service tunnels while Dara burns her own archives to buy time — destroying twenty years of her work to protect one truth. Casper escapes with the testimony core but loses Dara to arrest. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of keeping records.

chapters.title: Nineteen Hours
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The final jump window opens in nineteen hours and closes forever; after that, no civilian ship reaches Halcyon for a year — enough time for every witness to disappear. The ship is damaged, the crew exhausted, and the compliance module is broadcasting their position. Beat: the darkest hour, stated plainly.

chapters.title: What Casper Would Keep
chapters.summary: Iyo offers a terrible option: the Vespera's anomalous drive could make the jump early, but the exposure would age-forward everyone aboard — possibly fatally, certainly erasing recent memories, including the testimony unless it's hard-copied first. Casper realizes she'd lose the memories of her brother's voice. Beat: identity versus memory; choosing which self survives.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Instead of running, Casper uses the compliance module's uplink one last time — hijacking the Authority's own network to transmit the full testimony, the debris scans, and Dara's authentication to every colony on the Loop simultaneously. The silence between worlds breaks as ordinary people receive the massacre into their homes. Beat: climax; justice outside the law, delivered by the infrastructure of the lie.

chapters.title: The Jump
chapters.summary: With the truth loose and the Authority in chaos, the crew makes the anomalous jump anyway — not to escape punishment but to reach the tribunal before it can be dissolved. The exposure takes its toll: the crew ages forward past their true years, and Casper's recent memories blur. She wakes not knowing if she chose this. Beat: aftermath of courage, disorientation rendered tenderly.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the De-Aged
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. Nine witnesses with impossible bodies testify before a tribunal that can no longer pretend ignorance, because half the sector watched the broadcast. Verdicts land: the corporations are named, the record restored, Dara released. It is insufficient — no verdict resurrects the Kestrel — but it is real. Beat: justice as imperfect, public, and therefore alive.

chapters.title: Opening the Hold
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, final chapter. Standing before her brother's backup pod, she chooses not to restore him. She plays his recorded voice once, then lets the pod power down and buries it at the relay site alongside the Kestrel's recovered hull plate. Some things should be remembered, not kept. She plots a new route — to worlds that have started speaking again. Beat: resolution; mourning completed, identity chosen rather than archived.
